newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia military warns against poll pamphlets.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia military warns against poll pamphlets.

text.p: Indonesia's armed forces commander said authorities will deal harshly with people who distribute illegal pamphlets aimed at disrupting general elections on May 29, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Tuesday.

"The distribution of illegal pamphlets by people who want to disrupt the general elections is considered subversion. We will quickly take action in accordance with the law," General Feisal Tanjung was quoted as telling reporters on Monday in Semarang, capital of Central Java.
The paper gave no further details. Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.

The military in West Java is searching for people suspected of producing at least 6,000 pamphlets asking Indonesians to boycott the general elections. The military believed about 200 of the pamphlets had been distributed.
In Jakarta, police were still questioning three university students accused of distributing pamphlets whose contents criticised the government, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

Only three political parties are allowed to put up candidates for elections in Indonesia and some voters have stayed away from previous polls in protest. The government has banned any encouragement for people not to vote.
The Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Tuesday that Interior Minister Yogie Memet said people who refuse to vote or encourage other people not to vote were irresponsible citizens.
"Don't follow the wrong people. Follow the government. Those who do not vote are irresponsible," he was quoted as saying on Monday.
